value.alt: The Nexus framework as a flow from left to right. A Product Backlog, with a looping arrow labelled Cross-Team Refinement, feeds Nexus Sprint Planning, which produces the Nexus Sprint Backlog. That flows into a large ring labelled 3-9 Scrum Teams, holding several teams around a triangle marked Integrated Work. Beside the ring are the Nexus Integration Team, joined to it by a two-way arrow, and the Nexus Daily Scrum with the teams’ Daily Scrums. The ring feeds the Integrated Increment, then the Nexus Sprint Review. Arrows return from the Nexus Sprint Review to the Product Backlog and, through the Nexus Sprint Retrospective, to Nexus Sprint Planning.
value.credit: Scrum.org, The Nexus Guide (January 2021), Figure 1: The Nexus Framework, p. 5

value: A misses the guide’s warning that internal-only goals may not help customers. C overstates: the guide allows such goals but says to keep CV and UV in view. D treats inputs as value, which the guide says do not correlate with it.

value: The EBM Guide warns that improving only A2I and T2M without monitoring CV and UV focuses on internal processes, and can signal a lack of outcome-based goals.

value: When an organization targets improvements only in A2I and T2M without monitoring CV and UV, they are focused only on internal processes that may not help them further satisfy customers or achieve value. This can lead to, or be an indication of, a lack of outcome-based goals.

value: B contradicts the guide: the whole feature need not be built to judge its value. A relies on opinion, and the guide says beliefs about value stay assumptions until customers validate them. D delays learning without testing anything.
reason: "A leaves the belief an assumption" reads awkwardly; the guide's words (p. 7) are "beliefs in what is valuable are merely assumptions until they are validated by customers".
